source.publication: 2025 NJ-1040 Instructions (with GIT-1 & 2 Retirement Income, January 2026, and njit6/njit7 web pages where named)
source.section: Form NJ-1040 lines 15, 16a, 20a, 27, 28a, 28b, 29: Instr PDF p.21 line 27, PDF p.22 line 28a (Line A, Line B and chart), PDF p.22 line 28b and PDF p.23 Worksheet D lines 1-9 (lines 4-8: lines 15, 18, 21 and 22 added; 'Is the amount on line 8 MORE than $3,000?') with the Maximum Exclusion chart, PDF p.22 line 29; GIT-1 & 2 p.23 condition 3 (earned income 'combined if filing jointly' must be $3,000 or less); PDF p.8 lines 6-7 (regular and senior 65+ exemptions), PDF p.9 line 13, PDF p.25 line 30, PDF p.27 lines 38-39, PDF p.33 lines 42-43, PDF p.65 Tax Rate Schedules

worked: Federal AGI 93,000.00 (wages 3,000.00 + private pension 20,000.00 + interest 70,000.00); federal taxable income = 93,000.00 - 15,750.00 federal standard deduction = 77,250.00 (given, not tested; age 64, so no age-65 amount; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Line 15 wages 3,000.00 + line 16a interest 70,000.00 + line 20a pension 20,000.00 = line 27 total income 93,000.00 (projection: federal AGI 93,000.00 less taxable Social Security 0.00); measure 93,000.00, in the 0-100,000 band (keep share 1). Line 28a: age 64; Line A 20,000.00, Line B 75,000.00; lesser = 20,000.00. Worksheet D: line 27 is not more than 150,000; line 1 maximum 75,000.00 - line 2 20,000.00 = line 3 55,000.00 (more than 0); line 4 (line 15 wages) 3,000.00 + lines 5-7 (business, partnership, S corporation) 0.00 = line 8 3,000.00, which is not MORE than 3,000, so she continues to line 9: unclaimed exclusion 55,000.00, less than her remaining income of 73,000.00, so line 28b = 55,000.00 (projection: earned income, wages plus self-employment, 3,000.00 is at the 3,000 per-return limit, so the relief applies; room 75,000 - 20,000 = 55,000.00, covered interest 70,000.00, lesser 55,000.00; the cap binds, so the booklet's coverage of wages makes no difference here). Line 28c = 75,000.00, the single maximum. Line 29 New Jersey gross income = 93,000.00 - 20,000.00 - 55,000.00 = 18,000.00. Line 30 exemptions (line 13): regular 1,000 x 1 (nobody is 65 or older, so no senior exemption) = 1,000.00; line 38 = 1,000.00 (no other deductions). Line 39/42 taxable income = 18,000.00 - 1,000.00 = 17,000.00. Line 43 tax, rate schedule Table A (single/separate) as bands: 17,000.00 x 0.014 = 238.00. The booklet's Tax Table (taxable income under 100,000) gives 238 for the 17,000-17,050 row (schedule at the midpoint 17,025, rounded); expected keeps the exact schedule result. No credits. State income tax = 238.00. The pension is noncontributory, so the New Jersey taxable amount (line 20a) equals the federal taxable amount and line 20b is empty.
accepted_approximations: Tax Table: for taxable income under 100,000 New Jersey uses its Tax Table, the schedule's tax at each 50-dollar row's midpoint rounded to the dollar; the projection uses the exact schedule.
